target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted first but the local OpenAI API key is rejected with 401, so it could not produce a review.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.
- No `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is available in this environment. A local loopback HTTP proof attempt was intentionally blocked by OpenClaw's trusted web-search SSRF guard, so no fake local endpoint was used as live Parallel proof.
